text: Ah. The auditor. Jonah Pell; I am what passes for a hospital. Please do not touch the scanner arch, it sulks.
Medically? Ten people, all underfed, all overtired, none of them willing to admit either. I can treat most things. What I cannot treat is a cabinet that keeps emptying itself.

choices.text: How bad is the crew's health, honestly?

text: Six stim injectors in two months. I dispense perhaps one a year. Somebody on this station is keeping themselves awake on purpose, and whoever it is did not come to me.
I am a doctor, not a detective, and they all clam up when I ask. They might talk to a stranger with a datapad.

health.text: Chronic fatigue across the board. Tuck is the worst: I would ground him if I could find anyone else to run the bore. Dr. Suvari has stopped coming to her check-ups, which is its own diagnosis. And the Administrator is running on willpower, which is not a food group.

variants.text: Breathe slowly. The scrubbers are losing. I have people coming in with headaches every hour.
Sit down before you fall down. You look worse than my patients.
No power to the beds. I am practising medicine by lamplight like a ship's surgeon.

choices.text: It is Tuck taking the stims.
The stims were a clerical error. Dex mis-shelved a crate.
Tuck cannot sleep. Is there something gentler than stims?
I trained as a medic. Let me carry a cabinet key.
choices.if: background() == 'medic' and not has_item('keycard_med') and rel() >= 10

choices.text: What do you make of the dig?

variants.text: Hold still. ...There. An hour under the arch and you will pass for healthy.
The arch is dark, so this is needle and thread. It will hold. It will also hurt.

text: Tuck. Of course it is Tuck. And he has been buying them, which means somebody has been selling my stock back to my own patients.
I am pulling him off the bore. He will hate me. He would hate dying of a cardiac event rather more.

lie_ok.text: A mis-shelved crate. ...That is suspiciously tidy. But I would rather believe it than not. Thank you for looking. Here, for your trouble.

lie_fail.text: I have been lied to by patients for thirty years, Auditor. You are not even in the top hundred. Who is it?

sedative.text: If he would only have come to me... Here. Two doses. They will not stop whatever he is dreaming, but they will let him sleep through it. Tell him it is from a friend. He does not have to know which.

key.text: A colleague. On Tethys. I had forgotten what that felt like. Take the spare - and log what you take, or I will revoke it and your good name together.

dig.text: I have two patients with identical complaints: pressure behind the eyes, broken sleep, a sense of being... addressed. One runs the bore and one runs the lab. I do not have a word for it. Medicine tends to notice things before it can name them.
